trustBoundary: A structured transcription of the numbered AS Level syllabus outcome identifiers and learning scope. It is not a lesson bank, assessment bank, complete teaching sequence, or proof that Shadecode currently teaches these outcomes. Independently review against the official PDF before marking content complete.

topics.title: Basic economic ideas and resource allocation
subtopics: Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost
Explain scarcity as the fundamental economic problem.
Explain why individuals, firms and governments make choices.
Define opportunity cost and explain how it arises from choices.
Explain the basic resource-allocation questions: what, how and for whom to produce.
Economic methodology
Explain economics as a social science.
Distinguish positive statements from normative statements and facts from value judgements.
Explain ceteris paribus.
Distinguish short run, long run and very long run.
Factors of production
Define land, labour, capital and enterprise.
Distinguish human capital from physical capital.
Identify rewards to each factor of production.
Explain division of labour and specialisation.
Explain the entrepreneur's role in risk-taking and organising other factors.
Resource allocation in different economic systems
Explain decision-making in market, planned and mixed economies.
Explain how resources are allocated in each system.
Production possibility curves
Explain and draw a production possibility curve.
Explain constant and increasing opportunity cost using PPC shape.
Explain causes and consequences of PPC shifts.
Interpret points on, inside and outside a PPC.
Classification of goods and services
Define free goods and private economic goods.
Define public goods.
Explain merit goods and under-consumption arising from imperfect market information.
Explain demerit goods and over-consumption arising from imperfect market information.

topics.title: The price system and the microeconomy
subtopics: Demand and supply curves
Define effective demand.
Distinguish individual and market demand and supply.
Explain determinants of demand and supply.
Explain factors causing demand-curve and supply-curve shifts.
Distinguish a curve shift from movement along a curve.
Price elasticity, income elasticity and cross elasticity of demand
Define PED, YED and XED.
Use formulae to calculate PED, YED and XED.
Interpret relative percentage changes and the size and sign of each coefficient.
Classify elasticity: perfectly elastic, elastic, unitary, inelastic and perfectly inelastic.
Explain variation in elasticity along a straight-line demand curve.
Explain factors affecting PED, YED and XED.
Explain the relationship between PED and total expenditure.
Apply elasticity measures to decision-making.
Price elasticity of supply
Define PES.
Calculate PES using the formula.
Interpret relative percentage changes and the size and sign of PES.
Explain factors affecting PES.
Explain implications for how quickly and easily firms respond to changed market conditions.
The interaction of demand and supply
Define market equilibrium and disequilibrium.
Analyse effects of demand and supply shifts on equilibrium price and quantity.
Explain joint demand (complements), alternative demand (substitutes), derived demand and joint supply.
Explain price's resource-allocation functions: rationing, signalling/transmission of preferences and incentivising.
Consumer and producer surplus
Explain consumer surplus and its significance.
Explain producer surplus and its significance.
Explain causes of changes in consumer and producer surplus.
Explain how PED and PES affect the extent of surplus changes.

topics.title: Government microeconomic intervention
subtopics: Reasons for government intervention in markets
Explain intervention to address non-provision of public goods.
Explain intervention to address over-consumption of demerit goods and under-consumption of merit goods.
Explain government price controls as a reason for intervention.
Methods and effects of government intervention in markets
Analyse impact and incidence of specific indirect taxes.
Analyse impact and incidence of subsidies.
Explain direct provision of goods and services.
Analyse maximum and minimum prices.
Explain buffer stock schemes.
Explain provision of information as an intervention method.
Addressing income and wealth inequality
Distinguish income as a flow from wealth as a stock.
Explain measurement of inequality using the Gini coefficient; calculation is not required.
Explain economic reasons for income and wealth inequality.
Evaluate redistribution policies: minimum wage, transfer payments, progressive income taxes, inheritance and capital taxes, and state provision of essential goods and services.

topics.title: The macroeconomy
subtopics: National income statistics
Explain the meaning of national income.
Explain GDP, GNI and NNI as measures of national income.
Adjust measures from market prices to basic prices.
Adjust gross values to net values.
Introduction to the circular flow of income
Explain circular flow in closed and open economies, including flows between households, firms, government and the international economy.
Explain injections and leakages; multiplier is not required at this level.
Explain equilibrium and disequilibrium; marginal and average propensities are not required at this level.
Aggregate Demand and Aggregate Supply analysis
Define AD and explain its components using AD = C + I + G + (X − M).
Explain determinants of AD; detailed knowledge of AD components is not required.
Explain the downward-sloping AD curve and causes of shifts.
Define AS and explain its determinants.
Explain SRAS shape as an upward-sloping line or sweeping curve.
Explain LRAS as either a vertical line or a three-section curve (highly elastic, upward sloping, vertical).
Explain causes of SRAS and LRAS shifts.
Distinguish movements along from shifts in AD and AS.
Use AD/AS diagrams to establish equilibrium and determine real output, price level and employment.
Analyse effects of AD and AS shifts on real output, price level and employment.
Economic growth
Define economic growth.
Explain measurement of economic growth.
Distinguish nominal GDP growth from real GDP growth.
Explain causes of economic growth.
Analyse consequences of economic growth.
Unemployment
Define unemployment.
Explain measures of unemployment and difficulties in measurement.
Explain frictional, structural, cyclical, seasonal and technological unemployment, including causes.
Analyse consequences of unemployment.
Price stability
Define inflation, deflation and disinflation.
Explain CPI measurement and possible measurement difficulties.
Distinguish nominal money values from real data.
Explain demand-pull and cost-push inflation.
Analyse consequences of inflation.

topics.title: Government macroeconomic intervention
subtopics: Government macroeconomic policy objectives
Explain use of government policy to achieve price stability, low unemployment and economic growth. Policy conflicts and trade-offs are not required in this subtopic.
Fiscal policy
Explain a government budget.
Distinguish budget deficit from budget surplus.
Explain the meaning and significance of national debt.
Explain direct and indirect taxes, and progressive, regressive and proportional taxes.
Calculate and distinguish marginal and average tax rates (MRT and ART).
Explain reasons for taxation.
Distinguish capital/investment spending from current spending and explain reasons for government spending.
Distinguish expansionary from contractionary fiscal policy.
Use AD/AS analysis to evaluate effects of expansionary and contractionary fiscal policy on equilibrium national income, real output, price level and employment.
Monetary policy
Define monetary policy.
Explain interest rates, money supply and credit regulations as policy tools.
Distinguish expansionary from contractionary monetary policy.
Use AD/AS analysis to evaluate effects on equilibrium national income, real output, price level and employment.
Supply-side policy
Explain supply-side policy in terms of its effect on LRAS.
Explain objectives of increasing productivity and productive capacity.
Explain tools such as training, infrastructure development and support for technological improvement.
Use AD/AS analysis to evaluate effects on equilibrium national income, real output, price level and employment.

topics.title: International economic issues
subtopics: The reasons for international trade
Distinguish absolute advantage from comparative advantage.
Explain benefits of specialisation and free trade/trade liberalisation, including the trading possibility curve.
Explain exports, imports and terms of trade; measure terms of trade and explain causes and impacts of changes.
Explain limitations of absolute and comparative advantage theories.
Protectionism
Define protectionism in international trade.
Explain tariffs, import quotas, export subsidies, embargoes and excessive administrative burdens ('red tape'), including their impacts.
Evaluate arguments for and against protectionism.
Current account of the balance of payments
Identify current-account components: trade in goods, trade in services, primary income and secondary income.
Define balance, deficit and surplus in the current account.
Calculate balances of trade in goods, trade in services, goods and services, and the current account balance (CAB).
Explain causes of current-account imbalances.
Analyse consequences of current-account imbalances for domestic and external economies.
Exchange rates
Define exchange rate.
Explain determination of a floating exchange rate.
Distinguish depreciation from appreciation of a floating exchange rate.
Explain exchange-rate changes through demand and supply of currency.
Use AD/AS analysis to evaluate effects of exchange-rate changes on equilibrium national income, real output, price level and employment.
Policies to correct imbalances in the current account of the balance of payments
Explain the government policy objective of current-account stability.
Analyse effects of fiscal, monetary, supply-side and protectionist policies on the current account.

assessmentObjectives.AO1: Knowledge and understanding: recall facts, formulae and definitions; explain concepts with examples; apply knowledge to economic information in written, numerical and diagrammatic forms.
assessmentObjectives.AO2: Analysis: examine issues and relationships; select, interpret and organise written, numerical and diagrammatic information; identify patterns, causes and effects; explain consequences of changes in variables.
assessmentObjectives.AO3: Evaluation: recognise assumptions and model/data limitations; assess evidence and arguments; consider priorities and value judgements; communicate reasoned judgements and conclusions.

sections: B: one microeconomics essay from two choices, two parts, 20 marks
C: one macroeconomics essay from two choices, two parts, 20 marks

exclusionsAndCautions: Gini coefficient calculation is not required.
AS circular-flow multiplier is not required.
AS marginal and average propensities are not required.
Do not silently teach A Level-only depth as AS requirement.
